approach:
Add one reading check, `check_outcome_state(reading, request)`, to `crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs` as a `step!` line right after `check_governance_coverage`. It skips a reading with no capability, a question or no deliverables. It fires only for a delivery verb that is used as a verb AND has an audience-visible object or destination. This answers findings 1 and 2.

**Verb positions.** The verb is publish, deploy, share or release. It must stand at a segment start, after a list marker (`2)`, `(a)`, `1.`, `-`, `*`), or after a lead-in (`and`, `then`, `please`, `also`, `should`, `can you`, `could you`, `would you`, `want to`, `need to`, `like to`, `going to`). A segment starts at the first word, after a newline, or after `.!?:;` followed by white space or the end of the text. A dot inside `crates.io` or `v1.2` does not start one. Finding 3 is answered with an explicit marker rule: a segment-start word that is digits or one letter, followed by `)` or `.` and white space, passes the segment start on to the next word.

**Audience-visible object.** One of these must follow the verb, within 5 words in the same segment, stopping at before/after/when/while/if/because/until/unless:
- an object noun from a short list: page(s), site, website, docs, documentation, explainer, guide, book, report, tutorial, article, dashboard, crate(s), package, binary, app, image, artifact;
- a version token `v<digits>`;
- a destination word: npm, pypi, docker, production, online, `github pages` (through `pages`);
- an audience word: team, everyone, colleagues, customers, stakeholders, readers, public.

A pronoun object (`it`, `them`, `these`, `those`) counts only if such a word appears earlier in the same segment. A first following word such as `notes`, `process`, `pipeline`, `workflow`, `checklist`, `candidate`, `date`, `plan`, `button`, `of` makes it a noun use, so it is not a delivery. Technical verb uses ('Release the lock before awaiting', 'Workers should share the HTTP client', 'Publish the event to the bus') match nothing and are accepted.

**Acceptance.** A delivery request is accepted when:
- (a) a criterion has a whole-word state phrase (`reachable`, `is served`, `served at`, `http 200`, `is live`, `available at https`, `opens in a browser`, `downloadable`, `can be downloaded`, `installable` and similar). `url`, `tag`, `link`, `page`, `can open`, `serves` and bare `available at` are not on the list (finding 5); or
- (b) every detected verb is named in an `out_of_scope` item as that verb or its -ing form, as a whole word, not followed by a noun-use word.

The error is one line naming the verb(s), a reachable URL, a served page, and the out_of_scope exit.

**Claim.** The claim is narrowed to what can be shown (finding 1). Only the g6vy request is available (quoted in this brief). The two other recorded requests are in `records/`, which the snapshot lacks. So the replay test uses a labelled stand-in text for 7bf8 and 0wtc, built from D94 and D152. The stand-ins are not evidence. The CHANGELOG, D161 and the doc comment say: the check covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs (g6vy, run on the request text quoted in the brief); 7bf8 and 0wtc are another class and their recorded requests were not replayed. The 5% is labelled an estimate.

**Other findings.**
- Finding 4: step 4 adds the new check to the `check_reading_acceptance` doc order list.
- Finding 6: D161 records that the check has no reader rule (reader budget 1997 of 2000, `READING_RULES` fixed at 6) and costs one re-read.

**Input forms the rule handles → corpus case ids.** I read `crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs`. It has no delivery-verb case today; the only delivery word is line 563.

decisions.choice: Put the check in reading acceptance as a `step!` line right after `check_governance_coverage` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`. It takes the request text as an argument.
decisions.reason: The fault starts where a reading is accepted: a delivery verb read as a narrow deliverable, with nothing comparing the criteria with the state the user observes. The governance refusal for a publish request names the missing workflow and is the more specific repair, so it stays first. The check reads only the criteria, out_of_scope and request, like the governance check, so it sits before the file-comparison checks. The corpus case `delivery-request-naming-a-workflow-fails-governance-first` pins that order.

rejected.why: Out of scope. Reader budget is 1997 of 2000 and the briefs test fixes 6 rules. The refusal text reaches the reader on the re-read.

rejected.option: Put the check first, or in the verifier
rejected.why: First would hide the governance refusal that names the workflow. The verifier sees the problem only after the producer has run.

rejected.option: A general glossary or figurative-term check

decisions.choice: Fire only when a delivery verb is used as a verb at a verb position AND something an audience sees follows it: an object noun from a short list, a version token, a destination or an audience word. A pronoun object needs such a word earlier in the segment. Any other use is not a delivery.
decisions.reason: Finding 2. In a code repository these four words are mostly technical verbs ('Release the lock before awaiting', 'Workers should share the HTTP client', 'Publish the event to the bus'). Asking for a reachable URL there is nonsense and wastes the single re-read. Requiring a visible object keeps the check on the g6vy shape. The cost is missed deliveries with an unlisted object, stated in D161.

rejected.option: Fire on any verb at a verb position, with only a noun-follower list
rejected.why: Handles noun uses but not technical verb senses, which are the larger group.

rejected.option: Detect the verb in any position
rejected.why: Many false refusals on nouns ('a share button', 'the release process').

rejected.option: Substring match anywhere in the request
rejected.why: Refuses 'Add release notes' and 'shared helpers' and cannot tell noun from verb.

decisions.choice: List markers are handled explicitly. A segment-start word that is a run of digits or one letter, followed by `)` or `.` and white space, passes the segment start to the next word. `-` and `*` markers and `1.` are covered by the newline or sentence-break rule. A sentence break needs `.!?:;` followed by white space or the end, so `crates.io` and `v1.2` do not break.
decisions.reason: Finding 3. The old rule marked only words after a newline or `.!?:;`, so `2) Deploy it` and `(a) Release v1` were not found. The test strings use object nouns, e.g. `2) Deploy the site`, because a bare `Deploy it` has no visible object.

rejected.option: Keep the old rule and drop the `2)` and `(a)` tests
rejected.why: The input forms must be handled, since the corpus maps number-paren and letter-paren forms.

decisions.choice: The state-phrase list is whole-word phrases that say the thing is reachable, served, live, downloadable or openable in a browser. Leave out `url`, `tag`, `link`, `page`, `can open`, `can be opened`, `serves` and bare `available at` or `accessible at`. Keep `available at https` and `available at http`.
decisions.reason: Findings (d) and 5. 'A reader can open docs/explainer.md' and 'docs/explainer.md is available at docs/' still describe only a file, which is the g6vy misread. Tests refuse both. The share test criterion becomes 'The shared link is reachable by the recipient'.

rejected.why: The reader sets the kind; a behavior criterion that only says a file exists would pass.

decisions.choice: The out_of_scope exit needs the verb or its -ing form (publish/publishing, deploy/deploying, share/sharing, release/releasing) as a whole word in an item, not followed by a noun-use word. When there are several verbs, each must be covered unless a criterion names a state.
decisions.reason: Finding (c) of the earlier job. A substring match let 'Changes to shared helpers' and 'Release notes are unchanged' satisfy the exit. `governance_is_covered` uses substring `contains`; this check does not reuse it.

decisions.choice: Claim only what is shown. The check covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs: g6vy, replayed on the request text quoted in the brief. The recorded requests of 7bf8 and 0wtc are not in the snapshot, so the replay test labels their text as stand-in (built from D94 and D152). The CHANGELOG, D161 and the doc comment say that these two requests were not replayed and are another class. The test asserts the caught set is {g6vy} and ties the CHANGELOG phrase `covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs` and the words `not replayed` to the computed count.
decisions.reason: Finding 1. Text the planner writes without delivery verbs cannot fail, so a measured '1 of 3' would rest on an assumption. The honest statement is a scope claim with one measured case. The g6vy text is labelled as quoted from the brief, since it may be only the first sentence of the real request.

rejected.option: Claim the whole misread class, or 3 of 3
Block the plan until the host copies the two recorded texts

decisions.reason: Nothing measured the rate; the records are absent from the snapshot. Finding 6 asks for the missing reader rule to be recorded.
